cases.title: An unknown aggregation output name is rejected at startup
cases.intent: An aggregation output that does not exist (here 'p95') would otherwise produce nothing. ScheduleConfiguration.validate validates its AggregationConfiguration, whose validateOutputName checks every output against the aggregation functions; this runs inside BaseConfiguration.validate, before any controller check. ServiceMain logs 'Error creating service instance because of configuration error' and exits with 1 (ServiceMain.kt:153, :173), before any schedule runs.

assert.text: Error creating service instance because of configuration error
Aggregation for source [sim], channel [ctr]
"p95" is not a valid aggregated value

assert.comment: The configuration is rejected before a service instance exists.

cases.intent: Channel Names become the keys of the output values map, so two channels named alike would overwrite each other. SourceConfiguration.validateUniqueChannelNames counts names (falling back to the ID) and rejects duplicates. ServiceMain logs 'Error creating service instance because of configuration error' and exits with 1 (ServiceMain.kt:153, :173), before any schedule runs.

cases.title: The documented 'absent' alias '&!' is rejected as a condition filter operator; only '!' and 'absent' are registered
cases.intent: docs/core/condition-filter-configuration.md:27 and :67 list '&!' as the alias of 'absent', but AbsentConditionFilter registers '!' (AbsentConditionFilter.kt:23), so a configuration copied from the docs does not start. FilterConfiguration.validate(builder) reports the operator and the valid list, which the case checks for '!' and 'absent'. The documentation is what is wrong here, so this is asserted as the current contract and reported, not pinned as a code defect. ServiceMain logs 'Error creating service instance because of configuration error' and exits with 1 (ServiceMain.kt:153, :173), before any schedule runs.

assert.text: Error creating service instance because of configuration error
Operator "&!" is not a valid filter operator, valid operators are
,#,present,!,absent,

assert.comment: The configuration is rejected before a service instance exists.

cases.title: Two store-forward targets that forward to each other are rejected as a sub-target loop
cases.intent: A target chain loop would forward a message forever. validateTargets walks every target's sub-targets, including targets no schedule uses, and rejects a target that appears in its own chain. SF1 and SF2 stay in sfc-main in IPC mode (ipcLocalTargets), as intermediate targets would. ServiceMain logs 'Error creating service instance because of configuration error' and exits with 1 (ServiceMain.kt:153, :173), before any schedule runs.

assert.text: Error creating service instance because of configuration error
Target "SF1" causes loop in sub target chain SF1 -> SF2 -> SF1

assert.comment: The configuration is rejected before a service instance exists.

cases.title: Loop detection rejects a diamond - two chains sharing a leaf - although it has no loop (known defect)
cases.intent: Fan-out to two intermediate targets that both deliver to one final target is a legitimate topology. walkTargets assigns each child's returned path back to targetPath (ControllerServiceConfiguration.kt:143), so after the first branch SF0 -> SFA -> LEAF the second branch starts from [SF0, SFA, LEAF] and LEAF is reported as a loop. None of these targets is used by the schedule, but every configured target is walked, so the whole configuration is refused and SFC exits 1. The gate accepts the exit (orExit, no fail-fast) so that a fixed SFC, which runs and writes, is judged by records instead. The store-forward targets stay in sfc-main in IPC mode.

knownDefect.summary: walkTargets reassigns targetPath with the child's accumulated path (ControllerServiceConfiguration.kt:143), so a second branch sees the first branch's descendants as ancestors and a diamond is rejected as a loop

assertCurrent.text: Target "LEAF" causes loop in sub target chain SF0 -> SFA -> LEAF -> SFB -> LEAF

texts: causes loop in sub target chain

cases.title: A transformation whose single operator is unknown is rejected at startup
cases.intent: An unknown operator name would otherwise null the channel at runtime. The transformation deserializer turns it into an InvalidTransformationOperator, and validateOperatorTypes reports it when it is the only operator of the transformation (an unknown operator inside a chain is a different, catalogued gap). ServiceMain logs 'Error creating service instance because of configuration error' and exits with 1 (ServiceMain.kt:153, :173), before any schedule runs.

assert.text: Error creating service instance because of configuration error
Transformation "T" is invalid
Transformation operator Nope is an invalid operator

assert.comment: The configuration is rejected before a service instance exists.
